headline: Interpretation makes sense of evidence—connecting observations to conclusions through reasoning
universal_truth: Data doesn't speak for itself; interpretation is where meaning comes from—and where bias enters
fun_facts: The same data can support different interpretations depending on framework used
Pre-existing beliefs strongly influence how we interpret new evidence
Scientists often disagree about what results mean even when they agree on the data
discussion_questions: How do your existing beliefs shape how you interpret new information?
When have you seen the same evidence interpreted differently by different people?
How do you check whether your interpretation is correct?

hook.script: Evidence doesn't interpret itself. Footprints in mud are just impressions—until someone concludes 'an animal walked here.' Interpretation bridges observation and conclusion. It's essential—and it's where bias enters.

cliff.script: We often jump from evidence to conclusion without noticing interpretation. Why is that step important to examine?

options.text: Interpretation is where meaning—and error—come from; data is just data until interpreted; recognizing interpretation as a step lets you question it and consider alternatives
options.response: Yes. Data says nothing until interpreted. Recognizing interpretation as a step makes it questionable. Different interpretations of the same data reveal where you're making inferences.
Some evidence is clear, but interpretation is often more contested than the evidence itself...

fact1.title: Data Plus Framework
fact1.script: Data enters a framework for interpretation. Change the framework, change the meaning. A fever means infection to a doctor, might mean teething to a parent. Same observation, different meanings.

fact2.title: Bias Entry Point
fact2.script: Interpretation is where bias enters. We interpret evidence to fit what we already believe. Recognizing this step helps you catch yourself making convenient interpretations.

fact3.title: Alternative Interpretations
fact3.script: Before committing to an interpretation, ask: 'What else could this mean?' Generate alternatives. Your first interpretation might be right—but it might also be comfortable.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Data doesn't speak for itself. Interpretation is where meaning comes from—and where bias enters. Question your interpretations.

outro.script: That's Day 298. Tomorrow, we'll explore explanations that keep working—theories. Until then, notice when you're interpreting and consider alternatives.

growTrack.title: Interpretation Check - What Else Could It Mean?
growTrack.activity: Think of a recent situation you interpreted a certain way. What evidence did you have? What was your interpretation? What are two alternative interpretations of the same evidence? How confident should you be in your reading?
